title: Why does the Qur'an forbid the smallest sound of irritation first?

beats.narration: Of all the ways to hurt your parents, the Qur'an forbids the smallest sound first. Why?
Not violence. Not abandonment. The verse reaches for the tiniest thing: when they grow old with you, don't even say uff — a clipped breath of irritation. Why legislate the minimum?
Because uff is not neutral. Elsewhere it is the exact word a son throws at his parents while rejecting everything they ask him to believe. It is contempt's first audible leak.
Seal the smallest leak, and everything coarser is sealed with it. The verse sets its watch on the instant the relationship inverts — when the parent becomes the one easy to sigh at.
